A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUBSAMPLE-MFQ research. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figure 3 report original constrained-exploration and Gaussian Squeeze simulations, including reward gaps, computation times, and cumulative rewards.

after.justification: Appendix B and Figure 2 retain those original simulation results. Their relocation does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: The core subsampled value iteration and randomized execution remain. However, v3 adds single-trajectory off-policy Q-learning from historical data (Appendix I, Equation 42) and removes both shared-randomness execution variants from v2 Appendix I, Algorithms 6-7.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate constrained exploration and Gaussian Squeeze with the same state/action spaces and 8-agent and 50-agent systems. The reward specification changes within retained Gaussian Squeeze coverage; the off-policy and continuous-space extensions introduce no evaluated datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same centralized/mean-field value-iteration benchmarks, including the k=n reference. Newly cited off-policy methods are not experimentally compared against SUBSAMPLE-MFQ.

E3.justification: The Gaussian Squeeze local reward changes from 4*1[si>sg] - 2*1[ai>sg] in Section 4.2 to si*exp(-(si-sg)^2/4) - max(si,ai) in Appendix B.2. Other reported simulation settings, including m=20, remain. This establishes a revised reported setting, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing analyses varying k to examine optimality gaps, runtime, and cumulative rewards are retained without new empirical ablations, robustness tests, or case studies. The new off-policy extension is theoretical.

E5.justification: The experimental figures retain identical error bars, with no added run counts, seeds, explanations of the bars, or significance tests. Revised theoretical probability bounds are assessed under T1.

E6.justification: All three plot images in v2 Figure 3 are identical to those in v3 Figure 2, retaining the same values, benchmarks, and trends. The revised Gaussian Squeeze reward description is not accompanied by updated reported outcomes, so no performance gain or loss is established.

T1.justification: v3 adds off-policy assumptions and guarantees in Appendix I, makes the main convergence guarantee explicitly probabilistic, and changes the theoretical sample exponent from k^(2.5+|Sl||Al|) to k^(3.5+|Sl||Al|). It substantively revises the data-processing statement. The rewritten continuous-space probability bound in Theorem 4.10 also differs from v2 Theorem 3.9 and is inconsistent with v3 Theorem J.5.

C1.justification: The central subsampling, computational-speedup, and O-tilde(1/sqrt(k)) convergence claims persist. v3 qualifies the main convergence claim as holding with high probability and adds a conclusion claim extending the decay to historical-data off-policy learning under additional assumptions.

C2.justification: v3 explains the generative-oracle limitation and coverage/ergodicity conditions for its off-policy alternative. It introduces a model-specific interpretation of TV data processing while removing v2's shared-randomness failure discussion and explicit fairness limitation. The main accuracy-versus-computation interpretation remains.

D1.justification: New Appendix I specifies behavior-policy trajectory collection and a constant-step-size constraint involving mixing time (Theorem I.4). The Gaussian Squeeze reward specification is revised. Existing hardware disclosure, simulation sample counts, and stable-learning implementation are retained; no code or data release is added.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused off-policy/stochastic-approximation discussion citing Chen et al. (2021a, 2021b, 2025) and Fujimoto et al. (2019), among other citation changes. References associated with removed derandomization and fairness discussions disappear. The principal positioning against mean-field and localized MARL remains.

P1.justification: v3 extensively reorganizes the exposition: related work moves into the introduction, algorithm and theory receive separate sections, experiments move to Appendix B, and the appendix roadmap is expanded and corrected. The main-text algorithm overview and theoretical exposition are expanded and rewritten.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Motivating diagrams are merged into Figure 1, two learning algorithms are combined into one display, experimental plots move to Appendix B, and shared-randomness pseudocode is removed. Table, caption, and equation layouts are reformatted; the experimental plots themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies the main guarantee's probability qualification and adds an off-policy route around v2's generative-oracle limitation. However, Theorem 4.10 replaces v2's product-form probability bound with 1+200/k-201/(200*sqrt(k)), which can exceed 1 and contradicts Theorem J.5. The new remark after Lemma E.8 also incorrectly excludes TV from f-divergences. These benefits and regressions in theoretical reliability prevent a confident net quality judgment.
